text:
Alex: Quick thought — what if we use a similarity heuristic to coalesce nearby prefixes into a shared slab before eviction to reduce churn? small idea, outline below.
Mira: interesting. need concrete on similarity metric — time-window + access pattern or token-prefix affinity?
Alex: time-window + bloom of recent keys + weighted access frequency. if overlap > 0.7 we treat as candidate for coalescing.
Sam: how does this interact with lease/ownership? coalescing implies multiple tenants might share slab -> safety concerns.
Alex: plan is: coalesce only within same tenant or same isolation group. cross-tenant only if explicit opt-in and quota-tagged.
Jordan: can you sketch the handoff flow? worried about read-after-write and tombstone visibility.
Alex: sketch: 
```proto
1) mark candidate set with candidate_id
2) pause eviction on those prefixes
3) create coalesced slab snapshot (copy pointers, not data)
4) update lease metadata: slab_id -> candidate_id
5) resume normal ops; eviction treats candidate as unit
```
Mira: pause eviction sounds dangerous for hotsets. what's timeout/backpressure?
Alex: short window (<200ms) and we do incremental snapshot. if snapshot fails we revert metadata atomically.
Linh: telemetry requirements? we should gate rollout on two metrics: eviction churn rate and tail latency.
Sam: agree. define thresholds: churn drop >=10% and 99p latency within 5% of baseline.
Jordan: rollback plan? feature flag + canary on single pool then ramp. also need deterministic test for read-after-write correctness.
Alex: tests: chaos test that simulates concurrent writes, snapshot revert, and lease reassigns. also unit for seq-numbers.
dev-bot: deploy-checklist: feature-flag, telemetry, smoke on staging, canary=1/10 machines, kill-retry tests, alert thresholds.
Mira: tradeoff: reduces eviction ops but increases complexity of snapshot metadata and corner-case code.
Sam: alternative simpler: use soft-affinity hints to scheduler instead of coalescing. less safe but simpler.
Alex: noted. I'm prototyping coalesce + incremental snapshot. will post RFC with diagrams and perf sims tomorrow :thumbsup:
Linh: +1 on RFC. include pseudocode for atomic metadata swap and metrics we'll publish.
Jordan: add a section about maintenance: how to break apart coalesced slabs when pattern changes.
Alex: will do. thanks all.
